questions.enonce_markdown:
Examine love as the central theme in I Corinthians 13.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In 1 Corinthians 12-14 Paul answers the Corinthians' disputes about spiritual gifts, especially speaking in tongues, which some treated as a mark of status. Chapter 13, between two chapters about gifts, says that love is the supreme way (12:31).

**1. Love is more important than gifts (13:1-3).** Even if Paul speaks in the tongues of humans and angels, has prophecy, knowledge and faith to move mountains, gives away all he has or hands over his body, without love he is "nothing" and gains nothing. Gifts and sacrifices have no value if they lack love.

**2. The qualities of love (13:4-7).** Love is patient and kind; it is not envious, boastful, arrogant or rude; it does not insist on its own way, is not irritable or resentful; it does not rejoice in wrongdoing but in the truth; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things and endures all things. These descriptions answer the faults of the Corinthians: jealousy, pride, division, selfishness and the abuse of the Lord's Supper.

**3. Love is permanent (13:8-13).** Prophecies, tongues and knowledge will end, because they are partial, but love never ends. Now we see "in a mirror, dimly", but then "face to face". Faith, hope and love remain, "and the greatest of these is love".

**4. Love in the whole letter.** The theme links with Paul's earlier appeals for unity (1-3), concern for the weaker conscience (8:1; "knowledge puffs up, but love builds up"), and order in worship (14:1: "pursue love").

**5. Love in Christian teaching.** The chapter reflects the teaching of Jesus on love of God and neighbour (Mark 12:28-31) and the new commandment (John 13:34), and Paul elsewhere names love first among the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22) and the fulfilment of the law (Romans 13:8-10).

**Conclusion.** Love is the central theme because it is the standard by which all gifts and actions are judged and the quality that makes the church a true body of Christ. Without it, the Corinthian church's gifts, knowledge and sacrifices were empty.
